title: Buy, Don’t Steal: The Economics of Cognitive Warfare
zh_title: 购买，不要偷窃：认知战的经济学
source: Small Wars Journal by Arizona State Univ
summary: 摘要 认知战以个人数据为基础，而美国以低廉的价格出售大部分数据。这篇文章做了三件事：（1）中国为美国选民档案支付的价格； (2) 将其与秘密收集的记录成本进行比较； (3) 提出五项提高对手购买弹药成本的行动。中国购买美国选民数据并不是为了阅读它。它购买了用于瞄准引擎的原材料。商业广告花了二十年的时间来证明，足够大的个人数据池，通过预测模型运行，可以向人们传递不同的、量身定制的信息。
content:
摘要 认知战以个人数据为基础，而美国以低廉的价格出售大部分数据。这篇文章做了三件事：（1）中国为美国选民档案支付的价格； (2) 将其与秘密收集的记录成本进行比较； (3) 提出五项提高对手购买弹药成本的行动。中国购买美国选民数据并不是为了阅读它。它购买了用于瞄准引擎的原材料。商业广告花了二十年的时间来证明，足够大的个人数据池通过预测模型运行，可以向每个人传递不同的、量身定制的信息。将机器指向人们的恐惧和忠诚度而不是购物习惯，其结果就是认知战：通过数据精确地塑造人们的信念和决策方式的竞赛。该杂志的一篇配套文章认为，认知战是基于数据的，因此认知防御是从数据层开始的。这篇文章对那个战场进行了定价。白宫于 2026 年 7 月发布的一份解密记录显示，这些原材料几乎不需要花费任何成本，因为其中大部分都是合法出售的。获取的算术 在早期关于复合战争经济学的著作中，我提出了成本不对称比率，即对手的进攻单位成本除以防御者的反应成本，作为现代冲突中财政消耗的衡量标准。
一架“沙赫德”单向攻击无人机的成本约为 35,000 美元，根据谁的估计，其价格浮动为 15,000 美元，而国会研究服务处定价约为 400 万美元的爱国者拦截机。战略与国际研究中心 (CSIS) 在分析俄罗斯无人机袭击时，采用了同样的 35,000 美元中间值作为故意保守的数字。这种交换比对抗防守者的 100 比 1 更好。在该研究中，14 个典型威胁配对中的 12 个对攻击者有利。解密的材料允许在不同的领域进行相同的分析：情报获取。结果更糟：交易所对攻击者的支持更大。从购买数据的成本开始。美国每个州和哥伦比亚特区都会出售或发布其选民档案。加州将整个文件的费用上限为 100 美元，对于大约 2200 万条记录来说，相当于每个选民的千分之二美分。阿拉巴马州的收费最高，每个名字收费 1 美分，即全州范围内的名单收费约为 38,000 美元。 11 个州根本不收取任何费用，根据选举援助委员会 2020 年编制的数据，24 个州对全州范围内的文件收取 1 至 1,000 美元之间的费用。直接从各州收集的完整国家档案最多可达六位数。中国支付的费用比这个少。
解密文件中最清晰的文件是一份网络防御通知，记录了一名中国行为者于2022年1月从美国商业网站下载了六个州的选民档案，并声明该信息“可从商业网站公开下载”。没有国家费用，没有入侵，没有利用。边际获取成本是带宽和分析师时间。偷窃的成本是多少 这种隐蔽的替代方案有一个价格表，而且这一次是公开的。当司法部于 2025 年 3 月起诉 10 名中国公民代表中国政府进行黑客攻击时，指控文件中描述了承包商 i-Soon 向中国情报机构收取的每个电子邮件费用为 10,000 至 75,000 美元

【原文 English Original】
Abstract Cognitive warfare runs on personal data, and the United States sells much of that data for pennies. This essay does three things: (1) prices what China paid for American voter files; (2) compares that to the documented cost of covert collection; and (3) proposes five actions that raise an adversary’s cost to buy the ammunition. China did not buy American voter data to read it. It bought raw material for a targeting engine. Commercial advertising spent two decades proving that a large enough pool of personal data, run through predictive models, delivers a different, tailored message to each individual. Point that machinery at a population’s fears and loyalties instead of its shopping habits, and the result is cognitive warfare: the contest to shape what a people believes and how it decides, made precise by data. A companion essay in this journal argued that cognitive warfare runs on data, and that cognitive defense therefore begins at the data layer. This essay prices that battlefield. A declassified record that the White House released in July 2026 shows that the raw material cost almost nothing, because most of it was legally for sale. The Arithmetic of Acquisition In earlier work on compound warfare economics, I proposed the Cost Asymmetry Ratio, the adversary’s offensive unit cost divided by the defender’s response cost, as a measure of fiscal attrition in modern conflict. A Shahed one-way attack drone costs roughly $35,000, give or take $15,000 depending on whose estimate one credits, and forces a Patriot interceptor that the Congressional Research Service prices at roughly $4 million. The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) adopted that same $35,000 midpoint as a deliberately conservative figure when analyzing Russian drone strikes. The exchange runs better than 100-to-1 against the defender. In that study, 12 of 14 canonical threat pairings favor the attacker. The declassified materials permit the same analysis in a different domain: intelligence acquisition. The results are worse: the exchange favors the attacker by an even wider margin. Start with what the data costs to buy. Every US state and the District of Columbia sells or releases its voter file. California caps the fee for its entire file at $100, which for roughly 22 million records works out to about a two-thousandth of a cent per voter. Alabama, at the expensive end, charges one cent per name, or roughly $38,000 for its statewide list. Eleven states charge nothing at all, and according to Election Assistance Commission data compiled in 2020, 24 states charged between $1 and $1,000 for a statewide file. A complete national file assembled directly from the states runs to the low six figures at most. China paid less than that. The clearest document in the declassified release, a network-defense notice , records a Chinese actor downloading the voter files of six states from US commercial websites in January 2022 and states that the information “is publicly available for download from the commercial websites.” No state fee, no intrusion, no exploit. The marginal acquisition cost was bandwidth and analyst hours. What Stealing Costs The covert alternative has a price list, and for once it is public. When the Justice Department indicted 10 Chinese nationals in March 2025 for hacking on behalf of the Chinese government, the charging documents described the contractor i-Soon billing Chinese intelligence services between $10,000 and $75,000 for each email inbox it successfully compromised, with further payments for analyzing the contents. Leaked internal files from the same company, analyzed by SentinelOne in 2024, show data from a foreign ministry fetching roughly $55,000. i-Soon employed over 100 people and projected revenues near $75 million. Those are the discount rates for soft targets, accounts and networks protected by ordinary commercial security. Hard targets are devices and systems that can only be breached with novel unpublished exploits. The exploit brokers that supply state programs publish their bids: up to $7 million for a full-chain iPhone compromise, $5 million for Android. RAND’s study of zero-day vulnerabilities found a median useful life near seven years, which is the asset an intelligence service burns when an operation is discovered. Above all of it sits a national intelligence budget the Director of National Intelligence discloses only as a top line, $73.4 billion requested for fiscal 2025, with everything below that classified. Set the routes side by side. Ten thousand dollars per inbox is the cheapest documented rate for stealing personal data one target at a time. One hundred dollars buys the registration record of every voter in California. The asymmetry is three to four orders of magnitude in direct cost, and that is before risk is priced at all. Covert collection carries indictment, attribution, sanctions, and the loss of tools that took years to build. A commercial download carries none. The defender’s side of the ratio is worse still. Equifax agreed to a settlement of at least $575 million and potentially $700 million for a breach affecting 147 million people. UnitedHealth Group reported that the Change Healthcare attack would cost roughly $2.87 billion in 2024. A breach of the Office of Personnel Management compromised background investigation files on 21.5 million people, including 5.6 million sets of fingerprints, at a national security cost no settlement figure captures. On the kinetic battlefield, an attacker spends a dollar to force thousands. In the data domain, the attacker spends nothing to force billions, or, when the data is legally public, to force no response at all, because there is nothing to remediate and no one to indict. The Portfolio Is the Tell The declassified catalog of data held by a People’s Republic of China computer network exploitation actor around 2019 reads as my cost-asymmetry framework predicts. Most of its American entries are cheap or free: voter files, breached credentials circulating in criminal dumps, social media account data, the commodity substrate of identity resolution. A small number of entries fall into a different category: F-15 maintenance and technical manuals, and documents from four cleared defense contractors. Technical data tied to items on the United States Munitions List cannot be bought at any price, which is precisely why it was stolen. That split is what a rational collector produces. Commodity data is purchased or scraped because covert action against it would be economically irrational. Export-controlled technical data is stolen because no legal market exists. Expensive, risky tradecraft is reserved for the material money cannot buy. An intelligence service that behaves this way is optimizing, and the results of that optimization are reflected in the price column. This reframes how the July release should be read. The alarming interpretation, that a 2022 download of public records constitutes an election compromise, misprices the event. The economic interpretation is more troubling: the United States has structured its data environment so that the cheapest route to a national targeting file on the American population runs through lawful commerce. The vulnerability is not a firewall. It is a fee schedule. Why the Cheapest Input Buys the Most Influence Cognitive warfare is the effort to shape a population’s perceptions, judgments, and decisions. Congress ordered the Department of War to define it in the 2026 National Defense Authorization Act , a task still unfinished months past its deadline, and this journal has carried a sustained debate over whether the term describes anything new. Set the doctrinal argument aside, and the mechanism is one the advertising industry already built. Gather enough data on a person, model what moves them, and serve a message calibrated to that individual. Advertising technology runs this logic billions of times a day to sell products. A state with the same pool of data does it to sell doubt and division, one citizen at a time, and adversaries are already contesting that space with AI-generated content at scale. The declassified materials indicate that China reasons this way. Beside the voter files sits a plan to exploit American fault lines over race, immigration, and the pandemic response, and to push tailored narratives through social and traditional media. Traditional propaganda involves broadcasting one message to everyone and hoping it lands. A data-driven campaign delivers a different message to each person, measures who responds, and adjusts. The difference is the objective. A retailer wants a purchase. An adversary wants a belief. Here the implications for scale turn the economics from severe to alarming. A broadcast’s reach is capped by its cost. A data-driven influence campaign’s is not, because once the pool of data exists, the marginal cost of one more tailored message approaches zero. China assembled that pool for pennies. The input to one of the most consequential forms of modern influence, the shaping of a democratic population’s decisions, is the cheapest item on the battlefield. Inverting the Curve In the kinetic domain, the fix for a bad exchange ratio is a cheaper defense: a laser shot costing a few dollars against a drone costing tens of thousands. The data domain has an analog, and it is regulatory, not technical. Executive Order 14117 and the Justice Department’s Data Security Program , in force since April 2025, function as an export control on Americans’ bulk sensitive data, restricting transfers to six countries of concern. The economic effect is the point. The rule raises the adversary’s acquisition cost at the cheapest point on the curve, the legal purchase, and pushes collection back toward the covert route, where cost, risk, and attribution all favor the defender. A dollar of acquisition cost imposed at the point of sale buys more security than a dollar of breach response after the loss. From Arithmetic to Action: Five Recommendations Five actions raise the adversary’s cost to acquire the ammunition of cognitive warfare. First, extend and enforce the bulk-data transfer restrictions. Close the reseller and aggregation seams through which restricted categories leak, and fund the enforcement capacity to detect violations, since an unenforced export control prices at zero. Second, reprice public records for bulk machine access. This does not require closing them. Transparency for citizens, journalists, campaigns, and researchers can coexist with fees, identity verification, and rate limits calibrated to make wholesale foreign harvesting expensive and visible. A journalist checking a voter roll and a foreign actor downloading 51 jurisdictions are different acts, and the fee schedule should treat them differently. Third, harden the holders whose data cannot be bought. As the legal route closes, adversary covert spending will concentrate on cleared defense contractors, health systems, and genomic repositories. Security investment should follow that predicted shift rather than trail it. Fourth, extend acquisition-cost logic to minors’ data. Behavioral and biometric profiles built on children age into profiles of cleared analysts and field-grade officers, which makes children’s data the longest-dated asset in an adversary’s portfolio and the least defended. Fifth, measure defense by the adversary’s cost to acquire. Program evaluation across data security, foreign investment review, and privacy enforcement should report the acquisition cost imposed on a hostile collector, because that figure, rather than defender spending, predicts adversary behavior. The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States ( CFIUS ) and Federal Trade Commission children’s-privacy enforcement already generate the underlying data. Deterrence here comes from arithmetic, as it does against drones: make the cost to acquire this data exceed the influence it buys. Raising that cost is not only privacy protection, or even counterintelligence. It denies easy access to the ammunition needed for the fight over what Americans believe. Today the price runs in the opposite direction by orders of magnitude, and the adversary reads the price list as easily as we do. The cheapest weapon in the arsenal is the one aimed between our ears. A Note on Estimates and Sources Voter file figures are drawn from published state fee schedules; the national-assembly range is an inference, not an audited total. Covert collection prices are drawn from the March 2025 Justice Department indictment and from analysis of leaked contractor files. Remediation figures come from Federal Trade Commission settlement documents and Securities and Exchange Commission filings. The Cost Asymmetry Ratio framework is developed in The Cost Curve as Deterrent, with the simulator and data sources on GitHub. Disclaimer: The views expressed are the author’s own. The post Buy, Don’t Steal: The Economics of Cognitive Warfare appeared first on Small Wars Journal by Arizona State University .

title: What the US midterms mean for ties with China
zh_title: 美国中期选举对中美关系意味着什么
summary: 分析人士表示，民主党在本周的美国中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，控制了国会，这对最大竞争对手中国来说既是机遇也是挑战。 2026 年 11 月 3 日，在佐治亚州亚特兰大举行的美国中期选举之夜派对上，民主党人、亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 预计将赢得佐治亚州州长竞选，支持者欢呼雀跃。照片：Erik S. Lesser/法新社。投票结果让民主党有能力阻止唐纳德·特朗普总统特立独行的外交政策，投票结果可能会对特朗普产生以下影响：
content:
分析人士表示，民主党在本周的美国中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，控制了国会，这对最大竞争对手中国来说既是机遇也是挑战。 2026 年 11 月 3 日，在佐治亚州亚特兰大举行的美国中期选举之夜派对上，民主党人、亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 预计将赢得佐治亚州州长竞选，支持者欢呼雀跃。照片：Erik S. Lesser/法新社。这次投票的结果让民主党有能力阻止唐纳德·特朗普总统特立独行的外交政策，它可能会如何影响华盛顿和北京之间的棘手关系：关税会受到限制吗？分析人士表示，赢得美国国会参众两院的控制权使民主党能够限制特朗普在其任期结束后的两年内对中国产品随意征收关税。这可能对特朗普来说是一个潜在的打击，在双方达成休战协议（定于一月到期）之前，特朗普在激烈的美中贸易战中一直履行职责。上海复旦大学国际问题研究院院长吴心伯表示，如果民主党限制特朗普，这意味着他“在与中国的谈判中将更难利用关税卡”。 2026 年 5 月 14 日，中国国家主席习近平（右）和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在北京人民大会堂会面。照片：中国外交部发言人毛宁，来自 Facebook。
然而，民主党人还必须权衡他们的行动与特朗普关税在美国企业中的受欢迎程度。新加坡南洋理工大学拉惹勒南国际研究学院高级研究员德鲁·汤普森表示，国会将“在未来两年内利用一切机会阻挠（特朗普的政策）”。但汤普森表示，民主党仍需谨慎对待进一步限制关税，这些关税“受到工会、蓝领工人和小企业的欢迎……他们历来是民主党的基础选民”。华盛顿布鲁金斯学会外交政策研究员帕特里夏·金(Patricia Kim)表示，国会将“不太愿意支持那些会急剧升级对华压力的措施，如果这样做可能会增加美国消费者和企业的成本或增加冲突的可能性”。台湾是“游戏规则改变者”？凯投宏观(Capital Economics)首席经济学家尼尔·希林(Neil Shearing)表示，台湾问题可能会“改变游戏规则”。台湾是美国支持的民主岛屿，北京声称拥有主权。华盛顿是台北最重要的安全支持者，已向台湾出售了价值数十亿美元的武器，台湾将用这些武器抵御中国潜在的攻击。但特朗普今年五月宣称美国对台军售可能成为与中国谈判的筹码，这让美国的立场受到质疑。此后，他的政府将一批价值 140 亿美元的武器推迟了数月。
台湾总统赖清德于 2026 年 2 月 11 日在台北举行的国防预算新闻发布会上发表讲话。照片：台湾总统府。希林在一份报告中写道，中国可以利用特朗普总统任期的剩余两年加大对台湾的压力，特别是如果北京“判断华盛顿心烦意乱，或者特朗普愿意同意不干预的条款”。特朗普最近赞扬了他与中国国家主席习近平的“伟大友谊”，迄今为止，他顶住了民主党人和一些共和党议员的政治压力，

【原文 English Original】
A sweeping victory for Democrats in US midterm elections this week, giving them control of Congress, presents both an opportunity and challenge for top rival China, analysts say. Supporters cheer after the announcement that Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, former mayor of Atlanta, is projected to win the Georgia gubernatorial race during a US midterm election night party in Atlanta, Georgia, on November 3, 2026. Photo: Erik S. Lesser/AFP. Here is how the outcome of the vote, which offers the Democratic Party the power to stymie President Donald Trump’s maverick foreign policy, could impact the thorny relationship between Washington and Beijing: Will tariffs be limited? Winning control of both houses in the US Congress puts Democrats in a position to limit Trump’s liberal use of tariffs on Chinese products in the two years he has left in office, analysts say. That could be a potential blow to Trump, who has wielded duties throughout a frenzied US-China trade war before the two sides reached a truce, set to expire in January. If Democrats limit Trump, that means he “will be less able to leverage a tariff card in negotiations with China”, said Wu Xinbo, dean at the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai. China’s President Xi Jinping (right) and US President Donald Trump at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 14, 2026. Photo: Mao Ning Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson, via Facebook. However, Democrats will also have to weigh their actions against the popularity of Trump’s tariffs among US businesses. Congress will “take every opportunity to thwart (Trump’s policies) over the next two years”, said Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies at Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University. But Democrats will still have to tread carefully on further restricting tariffs that “are popular with unions, blue-collar workers and small businesses… who have historically been a base constituency for the Democrats”, Thompson said. Congress will be “less inclined to support measures that would sharply escalate pressure on China if doing so risks raising costs for American consumers and businesses or increasing the likelihood of conflict”, said Patricia Kim, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington. Taiwan a ‘game changer’? The issue of Taiwan, the US-backed democratic island claimed by Beijing, could be a “game changer”, said Neil Shearing, group chief economist at Capital Economics. Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer and has sold billions of dollars’ worth of arms to Taiwan that the island would use to fend off a potential Chinese attack. But Trump threw the US stance into question in May when he declared that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip in talks with China. His administration has since delayed for months a $14-billion batch of weapons . Taiwan President Lai Ching-te speaks during a press conference on the defence budget in Taipei on February 11, 2026. Photo: Taiwan’s Office of the President. China could use the remaining two years of Trump’s presidency to increase pressure on Taiwan, particularly if Beijing “judges that Washington is distracted or that Trump would be willing to agree terms to not intervene”, Shearing wrote in a note. Trump, who recently hailed his “great friendship” with China’s President Xi Jinping, has so far resisted political pressure from Democrats — and some Republican lawmakers — to greenlight the arms package. But a Democrat-controlled Congress “may force Trump to resume arms sales to Taiwan next year”, Wu said. “If that happens, that will also undermine the stability of US-China relationship.” Alternatively, for China, renewed support of Taipei from the US Congress may be “a stronger incentive for (Beijing) to play it safer with Taiwan”, said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute. Nevertheless, Thompson pointed out, while Congress can pass bills requiring Trump to approve an arms sale, the president retains the power to veto it “or simply ignore it”. Will Beijing treat Trump as a lame duck? From China’s perspective, even though Trump has been politically weakened by the midterms, Beijing is unlikely to change its strategy towards working with him, analysts say. “Beijing is likely to continue cultivating him through high-profile, leader-to-leader engagement with Xi Jinping, viewing this as the least costly way to manage relations with Washington,” said Kim. “Neither Beijing nor Washington appears to expect or seek a fundamental improvement in bilateral relations,” she added. Tsang of the SOAS China Institute said “Trump being relegated to lame-duck status will be used by the Chinese to put more pressure on him”. But, he added, Beijing is “calculating” and “would not want to push too hard and trigger Trump behaving totally irresponsibly”.

content:
Fundraiser by David Xia : Fighting for legal fairness
David Xia and 2 others are organizing this fundraiser.
Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)
Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.
Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.
Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.
Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.
Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.
Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.
Please contact Julia Lee and other volunteers through [email redacted] for the details.
We’re most grateful to your attention, encouragement, support and great help!
原北大教授、政治异议人士，现时政/财经新闻评论人夏业良先生（美国之音/自由亚洲电台/博讯/新唐人等媒体）因网络质疑和评论，而被中国逃亡商人郭文贵花钱组织围攻/抹黑，并在美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦法院提交所谓诽谤指控和滥诉。
夏先生通过电视节目和推特对郭的所谓爆料（包括最高机密信息）进行了质疑和批评，郭雇佣组织了对夏及其家人的网络围攻，同时指控夏对他进行诽谤并索赔五百万美元。
郭滥用美国司法资源， 目前正在进行中的诉讼超过41起，郭宣称他计划起诉至少91位对他进行诽谤的个人。
夏先生和其他被告均无力承担雇佣合格并有经验的律师之花费。因此在众多网络旁观者的建议下开始了募捐应对郭之诉讼的律师费用。
夏先生将把募捐得款只用于本案诉讼之中，并且得到若干志愿者的支持和帮助，他们协助收集募捐款项/记账与募捐监督等工作。本次募捐活动的目标已设定为十万美元，并且已经开设了一个名为“GoFundMe”之软件的募捐账户平台以作为主要募捐渠道。
请各位捐助者通过电子邮箱：[email redacted] 与Julia Lee等志愿者联系，以获得相关细节。

title: Chinas moon plan mirrors NASAs, except for one big difference
zh_title: 中国的登月计划与美国宇航局相似，但有一个很大的区别
summary: 中国计划在 2030 年将人类送上月球，这一计划与美国宇航局 (NASA) 的书面计划一致，但跳过了载人登月试飞，而是依靠机器人进行首次载人登陆的预演。据中国政府通讯社新华社报道，中国航天官员在 10 月 31 日于北京举行的第七届载人航天研讨会上阐述了他们的做法。据报道，跟踪中国太空计划的独立媒体 CNSpaceflight 发布的演示文稿中的一张幻灯片显示了两次无人乘坐的初始任务。 2027 年，机组人员将“梦舟”号太空舱送入地球轨道。
content:
中国计划在 2030 年将人类送上月球，这一计划与美国宇航局 (NASA) 的书面计划一致，但跳过了载人登月试飞，而是依靠机器人进行首次载人登陆的预演。据中国政府通讯社新华社报道，中国航天官员在 10 月 31 日于北京举行的第七届载人航天研讨会上阐述了他们的做法。据报道，跟踪中国太空计划的独立媒体 CNSpaceflight 发布的演示文稿中的一张幻灯片显示了两次无人乘坐的初始任务。 2027 年，机组人员驾驶“梦舟”号太空舱飞往地球轨道。然后由机器人接管。 “揽月”着陆器将于 2028 年自行着陆，无人载人任务将于 2029 年演练完整的着陆序列。“对于任何载人任务，我们都会首先尝试在无人状态下飞行，”中国探月工程总设计师王翔在中国官方电视台央视报道的英文字幕中表示。这种分裂切入了一场激烈的新太空竞赛的核心，并揭示了两种不同的制度文化。中国守口如瓶的军事项目依靠机器来证明其月球硬件的工作原理。 NASA 的民用计划利用人类试飞员，在公众视野中致力于在 2028 年首次实现宇航员着陆。美国领导人表示，他们正在恢复击败苏联登上月球的阿波罗剧本：让机组人员进行关键的试飞，经常发射，并在每次任务的基础上继续努力。
NASA 局长贾里德·艾萨克曼 (Jared Isaacman) 在 10 月 23 日的新闻发布会上表示：“这不是创业思维，也不是科技行业的精灵尘埃，也不是某种新的管理哲学。” “这是该机构非常熟悉的剧本——在短短九个月内从阿波罗 7 号溅落到阿波罗 11 号的剧本都是一样的。”另请参阅：新照片揭示了美国宇航局航天器从未见过的小行星景观 美国宇航局已经进行了其中一次载人试飞。阿尔忒弥斯二号于四月派遣四名宇航员绕月飞行。明年，阿耳忒弥斯三号的四名宇航员将在地球轨道上花费大约两周的时间练习将猎户座飞船与两个商业着陆器的测试版本对接的演习。一个着陆器来​​自蓝色起源，另一个来自 SpaceX。宇航员将爬进蓝色起源的着陆器检查其空气和生命支持系统，但只会与星舰短暂对接。此推文当前不可用。它可能正在加载或已被删除。今年早些时候，美国宇航局决定将这项测试作为一项单独的任务进行，在阿耳忒弥斯二号和首次载人登月之间进行。如果出现问题，“我们可以更快地回家”，美国宇航局阿耳忒弥斯计划的负责人杰里米·帕森斯解释道。阿波罗遵循大致相同的剧本。 1969 年 7 月，尼尔·阿姆斯特朗和巴兹·奥尔德林登陆月球之前进行了四次载人试飞。中国第一批登月宇航员将登陆月球。
尽管这些计划之间存在重大差异，但 NASA 也将依靠一些机器人技术。SpaceX 的目标是在 2027 年底之前将一艘无人驾驶星际飞船送上月球，蓝色起源公司正在阿耳忒弥斯 III 号之后进行自己的无人驾驶演示。美国宇航局将让这两个着陆器尽可能长时间地运行，然后再为其第一批宇航员挑选一个着陆器，而中国正在建造一个着陆器。在其他方面，这两个计划看起来很相似。两枚长征十号火箭将分别发射中国的太空舱和着陆器，两者将在绕月轨道上会合。然后三名机组人员中的两名将乘坐着陆器

【原文 English Original】
China's plan to land people on the moon by 2030 mirrors NASA 's on paper but skips crewed lunar test flights, trusting robotic rehearsals for its first human landing instead. Chinese space officials laid out their approach at the 7th Manned Space Symposium in Beijing on Oct. 31, according to Xinhua , the Chinese government's wire service. A slide reportedly from the presentation posted by CNSpaceflight, an independent outlet that tracks the Chinese space program, shows two of the initial missions with nobody aboard. A crew flies the Mengzhou, or "Dream Vessel," capsule to Earth orbit in 2027. Then the robots take over. The Lanyue, or "Embracing the Moon," lander touches down on its own in 2028, and an uncrewed mission rehearses the full landing sequence in 2029. "For any crewed mission, we will try to fly it in an unmanned state first," said Wang Xiang, chief designer of the Chinese lunar exploration program, in the English captions of a CCTV report , China's state-run broadcaster. The split cuts to the heart of a heated new space race and reveals two different institutional cultures. China's tight-lipped, military-run program trusts machines to prove its lunar hardware works. NASA's civilian program, working in public view to land astronauts first in 2028, leverages human test pilots. U.S. leaders say they're reviving the Apollo playbook that beat the Soviet Union to the moon: put crews on key test flights, launch often, and build on each mission . "It's not entrepreneurial thinking or tech industry pixie dust or some new management philosophy," said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman at a news conference on Oct. 23. "It's a playbook this agency knows really well — the same playbook that went from Apollo 7 splashdown to Apollo 11 in just nine months." SEE ALSO: New photo reveals an asteroid view that a NASA spacecraft never saw NASA has already flown one of those crewed test flights. Artemis II sent four astronauts around the moon in April. Next year, the four-person Artemis III crew will spend about two weeks in Earth orbit practicing maneuvers to dock the Orion spaceship with test versions of two commercial landers.  One lander is from Blue Origin, and the other is from SpaceX . Astronauts will climb into Blue Origin's lander to check its air and life-support systems, but will only briefly dock with Starship . This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. Earlier this year, NASA decided to do that test as a separate mission , shoehorned between Artemis II and the first crewed moon landing. If something goes wrong, "we can come home much more quickly," explained Jeremy Parsons, who manages NASA's Artemis program. Apollo followed roughly the same script. Four crewed test flights came before Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed in July 1969. China's first crew to head for the moon will be the one that lands. Despite this major difference between the plans, NASA will lean on some robotics, too. SpaceX aims to land an uncrewed Starship on the moon by the end of 2027, and Blue Origin is working on its own uncrewed demonstration after Artemis III. NASA will keep both landers in the running as long as possible before picking one for its first crew, while China is building a single lander. In other ways, the two plans look alike. Two Long March-10 rockets will launch China's capsule and lander separately, and the pair will link up in orbit around the moon. Two of the three crew members will then ride the lander to the surface and back. NASA's Orion carries four astronauts but also sends just two down. Blue Origin's lander even follows China's route, flying to lunar orbit on its own to meet the crew. SpaceX breaks the pattern, docking its Starship with Orion near Earth and pushing the spaceship to the moon. Left: Blue Origin A schematic of what Artemis IV's flight would look like with Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander. Credit: NASA infographic Right: SpaceX A schematic of Artemis IV paired with SpaceX's Starship moon lander. Credit: NASA infographic Want more science and tech news delivered straight to your inbox? Sign up for Mashable's Top Stories newsletter today. China says its uncrewed flights will make the first crewed landing safer. Its robotic lander also will gather some scientific data, measuring how hot the lunar surface gets and how the dust behaves. Its 2029 rehearsal will run every step, from docking in lunar orbit to landing, lifting off and docking again. The program has already completed early tests of its rocket, capsule, and lander. The race , Isaacman warned, "will be much closer than it ever needed to be," emphasizing that China has the spacecraft, landers, and a "credible two-launch architecture" to put taikonauts, the Chinese term for astronauts, on the moon within three years.  NASA's own deadlines have slipped repeatedly. Artemis first aimed for a 2024 landing, and Isaacman recently acknowledged that Artemis III was running about three months behind schedule.  He conceded that urgency has its limits: "No amount of my enthusiasm or schedule pressure changes the laws of physics."

10月，在海峡两岸颇受欢迎的台湾知名电视主持人蔡康永被媒体拍到出席竞选台北市市长的立委沉彪马的竞选活动。鉴于蔡英文在中国的受欢迎程度，他的出现很快引发了批评。现任台北市市长蒋万安邀请蔡英文参加他自己的竞选总部的落成典礼，从而化解了争议。在参加沉的竞选活动三周后，蔡英文公开表示，他从未支持台独，他的工作需要他与持有不同政治观点的人互动。第二天，他参加了蒋介石的竞选活动。
如果参加集会就等于宣布支持台湾的未来，想象一下11月28日的投票结果会如何。
执政的民进党候选人沉多年来一直在研究中国的影响力运作并促进台湾的平民准备。中国当局已以分裂国家罪名对他展开调查。国民党现任总统蒋介石在台北和上海的官员之间保持着开放的沟通渠道。北京和华盛顿可能会倾向于将沈氏的胜利解读为对独立的投票，或者将蒋介石的胜利解读为转向中国。然而，无论哪种解释都会将市政选举与台北选民未被要求投票的问题联系起来。
考虑一下沉和蒋 10 月 31 日辩论期间的一次交流。蒋要求沉解释为什么两个重建项目（一个在大同，另一个在内湖）陷入停滞。蒋将延误归因于台北松山机场附近建筑高度的限制。沉先生反驳了自己的问题：如果市政府官员知道这些限制，为什么他们不从一开始就向居民解释呢？蒋介石利用这次交流质疑他的挑战者对城市事务的指挥。反过来，沉用它来询问居民，如果他们发现障碍来得太晚而无法采取任何行动，那么专业知识对他们有什么好处。
然而，从他们激烈的交流中得到的最重要的收获不是候选人所说的话，而是他们没有说的话。中国这个两岸关系中的大象，在两个小时的辩论中一次也没有被作为关键问题提出。
这概括了台北选民实际做出决定时所依据的当地问题。有些人可能会投票给蒋，认为他推动了其他困难项目的进展，其中包括南机场夜市的一个项目。其他人可能会赞成沉的建议，即对旧建筑进行地震风险筛查并帮助居民安排维修。两个房主可以投票给不同的坦率

In October, well-known Taiwanese television host Kevin Tsai, popular on both sides of the Taiwan Strait, was spotted by the media attending a campaign event for Puma Shen, a legislator running for mayor of Taipei. Given Tsai’s popularity in China, his appearance quickly sparked criticism. The incumbent Taipei mayor, Chiang Wan-an, helped defuse the controversy by inviting Tsai to the opening of his own campaign headquarters. Three weeks after attending Shen’s campaign event, Tsai publicly stated that he had never supported Taiwanese independence and that his work required him to interact with people holding a range of political views. The following day, he attended Chiang’s campaign event.
If attending a rally is tantamount to declaring one’s support for Taiwan’s future, imagine what will be made of the November 28 vote.
Shen, the candidate of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), has spent years studying Chinese influence operations and promoting civilian preparedness in Taiwan. Chinese authorities have opened an investigation into him on allegations of secession. Chiang, the Kuomintang (KMT) incumbent, has maintained an open channel of communication between officials in Taipei and Shanghai. Beijing and Washington may be tempted to interpret a Shen victory as a vote for independence or a Chiang victory as a turn toward China. Either interpretation, however, would link a municipal election to an issue that Taipei’s voters have not been asked to vote on.
Consider an exchange during the October 31 debate between Shen and Chiang. Chiang challenged Shen to explain why two redevelopment projects, one in Datong and the other in Neihu, had stalled. Chiang attributed the delays to restrictions on building heights near Taipei’s Songshan Airport. Shen fired back with a question of his own: If city officials knew about these restrictions, why hadn’t they explained them to residents from the outset? Chiang used the exchange to question his challenger’s command of city affairs. Shen, in turn, used it to ask what good that expertise did residents if they learned about an obstacle too late to do anything about it.
The most important takeaway from their heated exchanges, however, is not what the candidates said, but what they left unsaid. China, the elephant in the room when it comes to cross-strait relations, was not raised even once as a key issue during the two-hour debate.
That encapsulates the kind of local issues Taipei voters will actually base their decision on. Some might vote for Chiang, crediting him with moving other difficult projects forward, including one at Nanjichang Night Market. Others might favor Shen’s proposal to screen older buildings for earthquake risks and to help residents arrange repairs. Two homeowners could vote for different candidates – while holding precisely the same views about China. The election night count offers no way to tell.
Taipei’s recent electoral history illustrates the limits of interpreting local elections through the lens of national politics – and vice versa. In 2022, the city elected Chiang as mayor. Just over a year later, in the presidential election, the DPP’s Lai Ching-te carried Taipei, edging out the KMT’s Hou Yu-ih by just 641 votes. Chiang’s mayoral victory would therefore have been a poor guide to the city’s presidential preferences. There is even less reason to interpret a vote in the capital as evidence of a broader change of heart across Taiwan for or against a political party – or that party’s approach to China.
True, the result will shape national politics. Winning Taipei would give Shen a larger audience for his work on civilian defense. A second term would give Chiang greater standing within the KMT to make the case for engagement with Shanghai, and possibly Beijing. Plus, the Taipei mayorship has in the past served as a launching pad for presidential ambitions. Winning office gives a politician the chance to advance causes that may have had little to do with why voters chose him.
The election’s outcome could certainly also influence cross-strait relations. During Chiang’s tenure, the Taipei–Shanghai Twin-City Forum has kept officials from the two cities in contact. A Chiang victory would give him another term to pursue those exchanges. A Shen victory would test the conditions under which they can continue. Although Shen has criticized the forum’s value, he has said he would attend if it offered practical benefits and came without political preconditions. On October 14, Beijing’s Taiwan Affairs Office dismissed his offer, citing his alleged support for independence.
Suppose Shen wins, repeats his offer, and finds Shanghai unwilling to meet with him. Concluding that Taipei voters chose to sever contact would erase Beijing’s role in the decision. The reverse inference – that vote for Chiang implies approval of his engagement with Chinese officials – would be equally questionable. A Taipei resident might value Chiang’s ability to keep municipal officials talking while still opposing closer political ties. Wanting the conversation with Shanghai to continue is entirely compatible with wanting Beijing to have less say in Taiwan’s affairs.
Local governance is undoubtedly important for the stability of the Taiwan Strait. Taipei’s city government, for example, helps residents prepare for an air raid, down to practicing how to reach shelter when the sirens sound. How well the city carries out that work matters regardless of which party holds power. Still, it’s not going to be an issue that is top of mind when Taipei residents fill out their ballots.
On November 28, Taipei’s voters will choose who takes responsibility for the safety of their homes, the city’s readiness for an emergency, and its dealings with Shanghai. Beijing and Washington have good reason to pay close attention to what the next mayor does with that authority. But anyone claiming a mandate for independence or unification is looking for evidence the mayoral count cannot provide.

content:
被监禁的香港民主活动人士黄之锋周四在承认串通外国势力罪后被判处 10 年监禁，这是他根据北京实施的国家安全法第二次被定罪。黄之锋.资料图片：HKFP。另请参阅：黄之锋在 30 多岁时寻求宽大处理，以获释，缓刑信显示 HKFP 收集了本地和国际反应。
当地反应：行政长官黄李家是“破坏香港繁荣稳定的罪魁祸首之一……黄志峰屡次触犯法律，包括组织、参与、煽动他人参加未经批准的集会、非法集会、藐视法庭等，表现出对法律的彻底漠视。”中国外交部发言人郭家琨表示，中国中央政府坚定支持香港特别行政区维护国家安全，依法惩治危害国家安全的行为。香港立法会发言人表示：“这个判刑充分体现了法治和正义，体现了根据香港国安法，任何企图危害国家安全的人都必然会依法受到严惩……针对黄志峰的证据确凿，他选择认罪……”对于国家和香港特区来说，他一定要抓住机会，学会如何尊重法律，正确认识自己的国家。”保安局局长邓克里斯表示：“那些对我们发动袭击的人，与黄、罗勾结的外部势力一模一样……他们必须受到强烈谴责，香港也应该受到谴责。”
推动社会变革的年轻人是任何充满活力的社会的财富，但香港政府却将他们关进监狱。”国际特赦组织副区域主任萨拉·布鲁克斯（Sarah Brooks）表示：“今天的判决再次严峻地提醒我们，香港的国家安全法如何成为惩罚异议的工具，而不是惩罚异见人士的工具。”

Jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment on Thursday after pleading guilty to conspiring to collude with foreign forces, his second conviction under a Beijing-imposed national security law. Joshua Wong. File photo: HKFP. See also: Joshua Wong sought leniency to be freed in his 30s, mitigation letter reveals HKFP rounds up local and international reactions. Local reactions: Chief Executive John Lee Wong was “among the primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong’s prosperity and stability… Wong Chi-fung has repeatedly broken the law, including organising, taking part in, and inciting others to take part in unauthorised assemblies, unlawful assemblies, and contempt of court, demonstrating his utter disregard for the law.” Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun “The central government of China firmly supports the Hong Kong SAR in safeguarding national security and punishing in accordance with the law acts that endanger national security.” Spokesperson for the Hong Kong Legislative Council “The sentence fully demonstrates the rule of law and justice, reflecting that under the Hong Kong National Security Law, anyone attempting to endanger national security will inevitably be severely punished in accordance with the law… [T]he evidence against Wong Chi-fung was conclusive and he chose to plead guilty…” Chief Superintendent of Police National Security Department Steve Li “I sincerely hope that for the rest of his time in prison, apart from reflecting on the wrongdoings he has done to the country and to the Hong Kong SAR, he must seize the opportunity to learn how to respect the law and properly understand his own country.” Secretary for Security Chris Tang “Those launching attacks against us are exactly the same external forces that Wong and Law attempted to collude… They must be strongly condemned, and Hong Kong citizens must recognise and acknowledge that clearly.” International reactions: European Union External Action Press Team: “The EU urges Chinese and the Hong Kong authorities to respect international legal commitments under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration and maintain space for political pluralism in line with the ‘one country, two systems’ principle.” Spokesperson for the UK Foreign Office “We call for an immediate end to all unjust prosecutions of individuals charged under the National Security Law and urge the authorities in China and Hong Kong to honour the rights and freedoms guaranteed to the people of Hong Kong under the Sino-British joint declaration (1984).” Spokesperson for the US Consulate “Wong has been unjustly imprisoned since December 2020, demonstrating that Beijing will go to extraordinary lengths to silence those who advocate for fundamental freedoms in Hong Kong.” Taiwan Presidential Office Spokesperson Karen Kuo “Seeking democracy should not be a crime, and young people should not have to sacrifice their freedom for their ideals.” NGOs Asia Director at Human Rights Watch Elaine Pearson “The harsh sentence on baseless charges against Joshua Wong is cruel and unjust. Young people promoting social change are an asset for any vibrant society, but the Hong Kong government puts them behind bars.” Deputy Regional Director for Amnesty International Sarah Brooks “Today’s sentence is another grim reminder of how Hong Kong’s National Security Law has become a tool to punish dissent rather than to genuinely protect national security… [it] cruelly – and perhaps deliberately – comes mere months before he would have been eligible for release under his previous conviction.”

As they expand in China, Europe’s companies are hollowing out Europe H.Seidl Fri, 11/06/2026 - 16:57 picture alliance / HPIC | stringer Comment Nov 06, 2026 5 min read As they expand in China, Europe’s companies are hollowing out Europe European companies are moving ever more parts of their value chains to China. Andreas Mischer says the EU must make sure this does not hollow out the region’s industrial base.  The ongoing drive of European companies to expand operations in China threatens European “derisking,” the reduction of economic dependencies and exposure to the country. Through “localization”, German companies in particular hope to gain better access to a huge market, insulate themselves from supply chain and other global business risks, and boost their competitiveness by lowering costs. But in doing so, they overlook that these advantages come at the expense of the EU’s industrial competitiveness. The EU needs to take action. German carmakers have been prominent proponents of an “in China, for China” strategy, localizing ever greater parts of the value chain in the country. Volkswagen built its largest research and development (R&D) center outside Germany in Hefei, China, to design car models tailored to the preferences of Chinese customers. Together with its Chinese partner Xpeng, the company has also been looking for ways to reduce the number of electronic control units in its locally designed and made cars. In combination with local suppliers joining the development process earlier, this is meant to reduce Volkswagen’s R&D costs in China by up to 50 percent. German carmakers seem to be fighting a losing battle in China But despite such aggressive localization drive, German carmakers seem to be fighting a losing battle in China. In the second quarter of 2026, Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, and BMW each saw sales slump by more than 30 percent year-on-year. Much of Volkswagen’s production capacity in China stands idle as a result. The company closed its Nanjing factory in 2025, after 17 years of operation with joint-venture partner SAIC. Estimates put utilization across all VW-SAIC’s factories that year at just 58 percent of a total annual capacity of 2.1 million cars.  With so much capacity sitting idle, foreign carmakers could be tempted to use their Chinese factories to make ever more cars for export. China’s recently published 15th Five-Year Plan for intelligent and connected vehicles already suggests that joint ventures between foreign and Chinese carmakers should concentrate more on exports. Should persistently declining sales in China make this option too tempting to resist, German and other European manufacturers would shift towards an export-oriented localization, adding to the flood of Chinese-made cars into Europe – and compounding their own problems in their home market.  Other German companies understand localization in China as a way to reduce business risk. BASF, which has cut 2,800 jobs at its headquarters in Ludwigshafen since 2024, inaugurated its EUR 8.7 billion integrated chemical plant in Zhanjiang in March 2026, the largest single investment in company history. BASF expects the complex to generate sales of EUR 5 billion by 2030 and to lift China’s share of its annual revenue to 20 percent. The country accounts for half of global chemicals demand but makes up only 14 percent of BASF’s sales. From this perspective, BASF is simply correcting China’s underrepresentation in its global business. But this purported risk reduction comes with risks of its own. BASF concedes that the Zhanjiang site will become profitable later than originally planned because China’s chemicals sector, like the car industry, is beset by overcapacity and low margins. The company believes Beijing will be able to stamp out so-called economic involution, yet the question is how quickly. Another worry is China’s recently revised national defense mobilization law, which allows the government to seize company assets in certain circumstances. As unlikely as this appears at present, geopolitical uncertainty makes it a possibility companies should from now on consider. Deepening localization in China is undermining Europe’s economic security A third group of German companies is deepening localization in China while reducing capacity at home. Virtually all major German car-parts suppliers are cutting jobs at home while expanding operations in China. Bosch plans to cut 22,000 jobs globally by 2030, many of them in Germany, while ZF Friedrichshafen wants to cut 14,000 jobs in Germany alone over the coming years. This comes as Volkswagen is also reducing capacity at home. Its plan to cut another 50,000 jobs and close up to four factories is the most prominent example of hollowing out of European industrial capacity and the growing threat of deindustrialization. Taken together, these corporate decisions and their consequences show that deepening localization in China is undermining Europe’s economic security and prosperity. In the past, companies built factories abroad to exploit greater economies of scale and generate profits that could be reinvested at home in R&D and well-paid, high-value jobs. Today, European companies that built factories in China are locally reinvesting the profit they make there while cutting jobs at home. As a result, boardroom decisions in Germany and elsewhere in Europe are increasingly coming into conflict with the region’s long-term economic interests. The EU should do more than protect Europe from Chinese overcapacity or make European companies diversify their supply chains. It also needs to start scrutinizing the investments European companies make abroad, in particular in China. The EU Commission, in 2025, asked member states to monitor their companies’ outbound investments in semiconductors, artificial intelligence and quantum technologies. EU leaders should now make screenings mandatory and expand this regime to more technologies and sectors. Further steps should follow, for example, making access to EU public funds conditional on retaining R&D and industrial capacity within Europe. 从蔡康永、《VIVANT》到姆巴佩：北京为何区别处理“辱华”事件？ - BBC News 中文
近几周，中国舆论场接连出现三宗被贴上“辱华”标签的争议：台湾艺人蔡康永、日本电视剧《VIVANT》以及法国足球明星姆巴佩。三宗事件看似性质相近，但官方反应、官媒投入程度和舆论热度并不一致。
蔡康永的言论被部分中国网民解读为涉及台湾主权立场，但官方回应有限，并未持续高调追击；《VIVANT》则引起中国外交部、国防部及官媒接连回应；姆巴佩事件在网络批评之外，更蔓延至品牌合作和商业层面。
三宗事件分别涉及台湾、日本和西方国家，却都被置于“辱华”的框架下讨论。多名受访学者认为，北京的处理方式并非单纯取决于对象来自哪个国家或地区，而在于事件是否触及主权、历史记忆等核心政治议题，以及当下的双边关系与内外政策考量。
他们指出，中国官方一方面持续借助民族主义凝聚国内共识，另一方面也试图控制动员强度，避免影响外交关系、经济利益和其他政策目标。三宗风波正好呈现出这种权衡与取舍。
蔡康永事件最初在社交媒体发酵。部分中国网民将其言论解读为涉及台湾主权立场，要求封杀并要求他表态，但官方和主流官媒并未持续追击。蔡康永多年来在中国累积的知名度与市场影响力，也使事件最终未升级为大规模政治风波。
相比之下，《VIVANT》引发的争议更为持久。剧中中国情报人员对日本特务施以酷刑的情节。事件曝光后，中国外交部、国防部等官方机构先后回应，官媒亦连日发表评论，相关话题一度长时间占据中国网络热搜。
香港浸会大学传播学院副教授闾丘露薇对BBC中文说，她和同事曾对外交部发言人的发言内容进行系统研究，结果显示官方态度首先取决于议题性质。涉及领土、主权、历史等核心利益的议题，措辞通常最严厉；如果牵涉日本，反应预期会更强硬。
她指出，其次是对象和双边关系。台湾被北京视为主权问题，官方没有退让空间；对日本，历史记忆和国内舆论令官方难以放软态度；对欧美，官方则要同时权衡经贸和外交关系，反应因此相对克制。
国立政治大学国家发展研究所副教授黄兆年认为，官方介入程度、回应层级和持续时间，主要取决于两个因素：事件本身在多大程度上关乎国家尊严和民族情感，以及事件发生期间是否存在其他重大顾虑。
他指出，对于同时出现的多宗争议，当局会进行成本效益评估。在蔡康永事件上，北京必须考虑台湾正值选举这一背景，也会担心强硬表态影响统派选情。
过去几年，这类风波的舆论压力往往不止停留在社交媒体，而是迅速扩散至商业领域。从品牌道歉、撤换代言人，到企业修改官网表述，中国庞大的消费市场已成为传递政治讯号的一部分。
另一场风波围绕姆巴佩展开。他被指曾发表涉及毛泽东的负面言论，引发中国网络舆论批评。
随着事件升温，多家与姆巴佩合作的品牌受到中国网民施压，要求作出表态。有中国品牌迅速解约、中止转播。官媒多次强调，中国广告收入是姆巴佩的重要收入来源，形容他“搬起石头砸自己的脚”，并以失去中国市场作为警告。
《VIVANT》则被新华社定性为“恶意抹黑中国、炮制虚假历史叙事”后，中国舆论场也开始追查哪些企业曾在剧中投放广告，并要求相关企业道歉。与该剧合作的日本企业三丽鸥（Sanrio）其后公开道歉，令事件进一步扩大至商业层面。
闾丘露薇认为，这种做法并不新鲜。“只要对方在乎中国市场，这种做法往往很快见效，例如品牌道歉、撤换代言人。”她说，这已成为中国对外施压的常用工具之一，而且未来仍可能持续使用。
不过，这种手段的效果取决于对方对中国市场的依赖程度。对依赖较低的国家或企业，作用有限；长远而言，也可能促使对方分散市场，减少对中国的依赖。
美国迈阿密大学（University of Miami）政治学教授金德芳（June Teufel Dreyer）表示，北京利用市场规模影响外部行为已有相当长的历史，而且在不少案例中确实取得效果。“如果一家企业认为失去中国市场将付出巨大代价，它通常会选择道歉或让步。”
但她也指出，近年一些国家和企业开始重新评估风险。当企业发现中国市场同时伴随政治和监管不确定性时，便可能寻求降低依赖。
美国企业研究所（American Enterprise Institute）高级研究员黄韵琪认为，民族主义动员与市场压力很难完全分开。“中国政府不一定需要直接下达行政命令，只要市场和舆论相信某家公司触碰了政治红线，企业往往就会主动作出调整。”
黄兆年则指出，与十年前相比，中国市场对全球企业仍然重要，但相对吸引力已不如过去。在地缘政治风险升高、供应链重组及中国经济放缓的背景下，企业的计算方式正在改变。对北京而言，市场规模仍是重要筹码，但未必像过去那样具有压倒性的威慑力。
受访学者认为，理解近年频繁出现的“辱华”风波，不能只从外交或对外关系角度观察，还要放回中国国内政治的脉络中。
闾丘露薇指出，以“百年屈辱”为核心的民族主义叙事并非近年才出现，而是在1989年后透过爱国主义教育，被系统性地推广至教科书、媒体和文化产品。她认为，这类动员首先服务于内政，核心作用是巩固执政合法性、凝聚社会共识；向外界传递政治讯号则属于次要功能。
黄兆年认为，在经济高速增长不再被视为理所当然的背景下，民族主义对中共的重要性正在上升。当局需要持续向民众展示自己是国家利益和民族尊严的捍卫者，而外部冲突和“辱华”争议恰好提供了这样的机会。
黄韵琪也表示，中国官方对相关事件的回应，往往不仅是针对事件本身，更是在向国内受众展示政府正在捍卫核心利益与国家尊严。她认为，民族主义已成为中国政府的重要政治资源。
不过，受访学者同时指出，民族主义不能无限制地被动员。黄韵琪警告，一旦民族主义情绪被全面激发，未必总能按照官方预期的方向发展。她形容，民族主义有时像被打开的“潘朵拉盒子”，既能成为动员社会的工具，也可能带来难以完全控制的后果。
近年愈来愈多“辱华”事件在网络上引发巨大讨论，却未必能在现实社会留下同样强烈的影响。在姆巴佩事件中，不少中国网民甚至不清楚争议源于哪一句言论；《VIVANT》的剧情争议对许多人而言较为遥远；蔡康永多年来累积的知名度和观众缘，也使部分用户没有完全响应抵制呼吁。
闾丘露薇部分认同民族主义动员出现疲劳的说法，但认为“疲劳”未必是最准确的描述。“我觉得更像是网络和现实成了两个平行的世界。”她说，演算法能决定人们在手机上看到什么，也能在短时间内点燃强烈情绪，但这些情绪往往来得快、去得也快。
在她看来，这更多反映民族主义动员的边际效应正在下降。“类似事件越来越频繁，议题又往往离普通人的生活很远，每一次动员的影响力自然就减弱了。”
抖音上也有用户留言说：“月薪三千累死累活到家，发现自己民族情感被伤害了？”这类声音反映，部分网民更在意现实生活压力，而非遥远的政治争议。
黄兆年认为，民族主义动员在中国长期存在，但普通人也会计算何时表态、表态到什么程度。并非每一次官方发动，民众都需要以同样的热情回应。
他指出，今天的中国人与其说是被“洗脑”，不如说是被“洗嘴”：人们对表达真实意见心存忌惮，但何时、在何种程度上响应中央，是一种计算，而非真的相信。

《国家器官》放映会揭露中国强摘器官行径(组图) 華府新聞 | 移植 | 人權 | 法輪大法 | 宗教 | 华府生活 |Alina Wang、筱敏| 看中国网
图片1：纪录片《国家器官》（State Organs）放映后，多位嘉宾就中国境内强摘器官的相关指控进行了探讨。由左至右依序为：法轮大法信息中心研究员Mark Yang；纪录片《国家器官》制片人宋美馨（Cindy Song）；《按需杀人》（Killed to Order）一书作者杨杰凯（Jan Jekielek）；“医生反对强摘器官组织”（Doctors Againvestst Forced Organ Harvesting）（Doctors Againvestst Forced Russo）博士；以及主持人斯坦塞尔（Amelia Stansell）——国际扶轮社第7610区“反对奴役行动小组”的主席。（摄影：筱敏/看中国） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
图片2：福尔斯彻奇（Falls Church）扶轮社社长里诺塞拉莱（Ricardo Noserale，右）与该社另外两名成员一同出席了放映活动，并与《按需杀戮》（Killed to Order）一书作者杨杰凯（Jan Jekielek）合影。（摄影：筱敏/看中国） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
【看中国2026年11月8日讯】(看中国记者Alina Wang、筱敏采访报导)获奖纪录片《国家器官》（State Organs）放映会10月29日在弗吉尼亚州福尔斯彻奇举行，吸引人权倡议者、医疗专业人士、研究人员及当地居民参与，共同探讨中共令人发指的强摘器官行径，以及如何克服让国际社会关注这一问题的种种挑战。
这场活动在乔治·C·马歇尔高中（George C.Marshall High School）举行，内容包括放映影片，及随后的专家座谈，其中探讨了中共对法轮功学员的迫害、幸存者所承受的心理影响，以及打击与器官移植相关的人权侵害的立法努力。
活动由泰森斯角扶轮社（Rotary Club of Tysons Corner）、7610地区反奴役行动小组（District 7610 Action Group Against Slavery），以及终止强制活摘器官扶轮卫星社（End Forced Organ Harvesting Rotary Satellite Club）共同主办。
《国家器官》于2024年上映，记录了两个中国家庭在长达20多年时间里，寻找失踪亲人的经历。他们的遭遇成为一项调查的基础，该调查探讨了有关中国模糊不透明的器官移植体系中，良心犯遭到锁定并被杀害以摘取器官的指控。
《国家器官》制片人宋美馨（Cindy Song）告诉现场观众，她拍摄这部纪录片的动机，源于她得知一些家庭的亲人在据称与中国当局接触后便离奇失踪。联合国（UN）人权专家以及美国国会的其他听证会，也曾记录类似的疑虑。
宋美馨讲述了一名17岁男孩的遭遇。男孩的家人原本认为，服兵役能为他带来更好的未来。据宋美馨表示，这名男孩遭到拘留、接受医学检查，之后因其器官被发现与高级官员的器官相匹配而遭到杀害。
她说：“我希望成为那些无法发声者的代言人。”她还谈到海外放映活动遭到干预的情况。2026年1月，中国驻巴黎大使馆据报向法国拉博勒（La Baule）的一家电影院施压，要求取消《国家器官》的放映。
根据法轮大法信息中心（Falun Dafa Information Center）的说法，使馆官员联系了电影院及当地政府官员，但市长拒绝介入，因此放映活动最终仍如期举行。
福尔斯彻奇扶轮社（Rotary Club of Falls Church）社长里诺塞拉莱（Ricardo Noserale）表示，影片中最令人心碎、最触动人心的片段，是那些家庭寻找孩子及亲人，而他们的亲人却再也没有从中国回来。
他向《看中国》（Vision Times）表示：“难以置信，这种事情竟然正在中国发生。”
来自弗吉尼亚州斯塔福德郡（Stafford County）的居民杰克（Jack）与儿子科尔特（Colt）一同观看了影片。杰克对于这一议题在美国主流媒体中受到的关注相对有限表示不满。他说：“我们在这个国家报导很多事情，但唯独这些事情却没有报导。”科尔特则形容这部纪录片“真的很棒”。
法轮大法信息中心研究员Mark Yang谈到了对法轮功的迫害。他表示，法轮功学员至今仍面临拘留、监视，以及被迫放弃信仰的压力。他还谈到海外倡议者所受到的威胁，包括他本人曾收到的恐吓讯息。
法轮功，又称法轮大法，是一种以“真、善、忍”为原则的精神修炼。尽管法轮功本质上是和平的，但中国共产党在时任党魁江泽民的指使下，于1999年7月发起了一场残酷的镇压运动，企图消灭这一修炼群体。当时，法轮功迅速普及，中共将其视为对其威权政权的威胁。
反强制活摘器官医生组织（Doctors Against Forced Organ Harvesting）心理健康顾问鲁索博士（Dr.Jessica Russo）谈到了那些认为自己可能成为器官摘取目标的人所承受的心理后果。
“想像一下，你身处拘留所，没有任何控制权，没有任何力量。你无法离开，而且有人以死亡威胁你。”鲁索表示，一些幸存者曾透露，在遭到拘留期间，他们接受了不明原因的血液检查及医学检查。调查人员对此提出疑虑，认为这些检查可能被用来评估器官配型。
鲁索还讲述了一名女性的经历。这名女性在差点遭到活摘器官后，成功逃离中国。她表示，这名女性花了数年时间，才逐渐从严重的心理创伤中恢复。
《按需杀戮》（Killed to Order）一书作者杨杰凯（Jan Jekielek），谈到了最初促使他调查系统性活摘器官问题的证据。
他回忆说，2005年和2006年开始出现相关报导，其中包括有关遭拘留法轮功学员的证词，以及中国器官移植等待时间异常短的情况。
杨杰凯指出，某些器官移植手术能够在几周内安排进行，这引发了人们对器官来源的严重质疑。尤其是，通常情况下，要找到器官配型相符的捐赠者并不容易，而且往往需要更长时间。
他也赞扬基层组织持续努力，让公众保持对这一问题的关注。他说：“我确实相信，基层的努力才是最重要的，也是最能够真正带来实际改变的地方。”
与此同时，中共当局否认有关强摘器官的指控，并坚称其器官移植体系是透过自愿捐赠运作的。然而，人权调查人员及倡议组织对这些说法提出质疑，并引用近20年来搜集的大量证据，包括目击者证词、与中国医院的通话录音、器官移植数据，以及一个独立法庭的调查结果。该法庭认定，良心犯曾遭到大规模强制活摘器官。
与会座谈嘉宾也讨论了《法轮功及强摘器官受害者保护法》（Falun Gong and Victims of Forced Organ Harvesting Protection Act），即S.4009法案。该法案已于9月28日在美国参议院获得全体一致通过。
这项立法将要求联邦政府提交有关中共强摘器官问题的报告，并授权对参与这一行径的人士实施定向制裁。目前，法案已送交众议院。众议员必须批准参议院修订后的版本，法案才能送交总统签署，正式成为法律。
主持这场座谈会、并参与反奴役倡议工作的斯坦塞尔（Amelia Stansell）告诉《看中国》，她参与这项工作的原因。
“我希望，如果有一天我和我的家人遭遇这样的事情，也会有人愿意冒着自身安危的风险来帮助我们，对吧？”斯坦塞尔说，希望借此活动提高公众对强制活摘器官问题的认识，并鼓励与会者组织更多放映、分享相关资讯，以及与议员接触，促使他们采取更具体的行动。
她说：“我相信，每一个人都是按照上帝的形象所造。无论信仰什么宗教，无论外表如何，我们每个人都有自己的价值。”

content:
花莲旅游新亮点：松园别馆、将军府浴火重生(组图) 建築 | 將軍府1936 | 任聿新 | 文学世界 |高妍晨| 看中国网
花莲松园别馆逆境重生，荣获第二届“台湾观光100亮点”，写下令人惊艳的篇章。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
2024年“0403地震”、7月底凯米强台接连重创花莲，观光一蹶不振。才挺过三年疫情营运压力的“松园别馆”满目疮痍，黯然停业；刚历经三年半修复的日式建筑群“将军府1936”，4月1日甫盛大开幕，不料两天后即遭强震，游客数直接归零。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
如今，花莲市区美仑溪畔这两个相邻的景点，逆境重生，分别荣获交通部观光署第一届、第二届“台湾观光100亮点”，写下令人惊艳的篇章。
兴建于1942年的松园别馆，以种植数十棵渡海来台的百年琉球松得名。
兴建于1942年的松园别馆，环境清幽，以种植数十棵渡海来台的百年琉球松而得名，旧称“花莲港陆军兵事部”。
因具制高点优势，能俯瞰美仑溪入海口和花莲港，又有松林遮蔽，隐密性佳，成为当时日军在花莲的重要军事指挥中心，也是花莲县仅存日治时期保留至今最完整的一栋军事建筑。
二战后期，战事吃紧，日本政府招募台籍日本兵成立神风特攻队（Kamikaze）。当时台湾共有4个神风特攻队基地。据说神风特攻队由花莲出航时，视死如归的队员们便在此聚会，度过出征前的“最后一夜”，而不幸罹难的队员则会化身白蝴蝶，守候在母亲和所爱之人身边。此传说为松园别馆增添一抹神秘的悲剧色彩。
每年举办的“太平洋诗歌节”，使松园别馆成为备受瞩目的诗文重地。
二战结束后，松园别馆曾作为美军顾问团军官休闲度假中心。其后历经二十余年荒废，又面临被拆除改建为观光饭店等危机，幸赖地方民众大力抢救，才得以保存下来。
松园别馆于1978年交由行政院退辅会管理，2000年开始大规模整修，2002年公告为历史建筑。2003年办理“洄澜国际艺术家创作营”，引领松园别馆朝向展览、讲座、工作坊等艺文活动发展。尤以每年11月间所举办的“太平洋诗歌节”最为知名，使松园别馆成为备受瞩目的诗文重地。
松园别馆营运团队积极抢救遭白蚁蛀蚀、松材线虫病害的珍贵老松。
松园别馆受灾休园后，经过整修，由退辅会重新招标，于2025年1月初再度开园。由营运团队与花东陶艺、金工等工艺师合作，提升文化定位，推出艺文展览和特色体验活动；还积极抢救遭到白蚁蛀蚀、松材线虫病害的珍贵老松。在营运团队群策群力下，游客人气回升，营运也渐趋稳定。
松园别馆园区郁郁葱葱，老松迎客，交织自然与历史之美，韵味十足。在木栈道上远眺波光粼粼的太平洋，欣赏诗情画意的溪畔风光，让人心旷神怡。
松园别馆古朴厚重的两层楼仿洋式拱廊建筑即为展览空间。
日式小木屋是传说神风特攻队出征前享用最后一餐、领受“御前酒”的地方。
松园香草餐坊贩售轻食和松针汁、松针咖啡等特色餐饮。
入园第一眼所见古朴厚重的两层楼仿洋式拱廊建筑即为展览空间；温润素雅的日式小木屋，就是传说神风特攻队出征前享用最后一餐、领受天皇赏赐“御前酒”的地方；生态池布满各种原生动、植物，蝉声、蛙鸣，颇为热闹；松园香草餐坊贩售轻食和松针汁、松针咖啡等特色餐饮。
徜徉松园之中，吹山风、听松涛、赏古迹，感受浓浓的艺术气息，追忆大时代的故事，也珍惜和平年代的可贵。
将军府是1936年日治时期花莲临港线最核心的军事日式宿舍建筑群。
位于美仑溪畔公园旁的“将军府1936”，建造于日治时期昭和11年（1936年），为当时花莲临港线最核心的军事日式宿舍建筑群，二战后作为国军眷舍。因年久失修，2020年获文化部再造历史现场计划经费挹注，是花莲规模最大的文化资产修复案。
顾名思义，“将军府”正是将军的住所。修复团队表示，当年有5位日籍高阶军官还留在此地，带领未归乡的士兵。开工前经沟通，仍有两位将军眷恋不舍，选择继续守护这片场域。
修复团队询问两位将军：“是否有哪个日子值得作为园区的纪念日？”出人意料的是，将军们认为10月25日“台湾光复节”，象征台湾这片土地开启新阶段，也代表不同族群间能有更深的交流和理解，值得珍惜。
“将军府1936”透着浓浓的日式风情，已跃升为“2026上半年花莲热门景点”排名第四的旅游新亮点。
整修后的“将军府1936”园区别致优雅。宿舍建筑群古朴温润，皆为和洋折衷样式的木造黑瓦，透着浓浓的日式风情。
芮氏规模7.2的强震虽未造成建筑群结构受损，但太鲁阁等指标性景点重创、道路中断，国旅市场瞬间雪崩。新进驻的在地餐饮、精致品牌业者原本预期的开幕蜜月期和清明连假人潮落空，前景黯淡，欲哭无泪。
“将军府1936”的经营团队携手在地跨界品牌，成立“洄澜好fun加值共创计划”联盟。
没有了太鲁阁，花莲观光还剩下什么？“将军府1936”的主理人任聿新说：“总不能天天坐在家里等人来吧？”“要一百万人来一次，还是要一万人来一百次？我选择后者。”
“将军府1936”的经营团队以伙伴携手“共好”的理念，梳理花莲温暖动人的故事。
任聿新和团队主动出击，携手在地跨界品牌，迅速成立“洄澜好fun加值共创计划”联盟。以伙伴携手“共好”的理念，规划体验活动，梳理花莲优质的餐饮、创作、渔村日常等成为温暖动人的故事，联结吃、住、玩的旅程，希望旅人能进行深度旅游，真正爱上花莲这片美丽的土地。
挺过漫漫复原路，经营团队展现的合作、勇气、韧性和坚持，令人感佩。（以上图片来源皆为摄影：高妍晨）
任聿新想要把“将军府1936”打造成一间属于花莲的客厅。因此，园区内所有特色名店，包括：家咖哩、定置渔场三代目、花莲县饼、喜欢采风、将军淬、OOA将军府X陈耀训‧面包埠……都和花莲土地、食材紧密相连，也努力诉说着属于花莲本土的故事。
好口碑带动好人气。根据“2026上半年花莲热门景点”游客统计，“将军府1936”已跃升为排名第四的旅游新亮点。挺过漫漫复原路，任聿新的远见、承担，和经营团队展现的勇气、合作、韧性和坚持，令人感佩。

Binance CFO is leaving to ‘pursue a new venture’ after $6.3 billion hack
Binance’s chief financial officer Kaiser Ng is leaving the cryptocurrency exchange.
According to Bloomberg, co-CEO Yi He said in a statement that Ng’s departure will allow him to “pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance,” and that a transition plan has been “implemented over the last half year.”
The announcement comes barely more than a week after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance users. The company froze withdrawals for several days; after accounts were unfrozen, users withdrew a net $3.6 billion in the first few hours.
Binance and the FBI blamed a North Korean group called TraderTraitor for the hack. The company also said that it would cover all losses, promising, “Binance will bear the financial impact of the stolen funds. These losses will not be passed on to users.”
Ng will be replaced as CFO by Justin Yek.

title: 林兆彬：中共真正懼怕的，是鏡子裡那個年輕的自己

content: 追光者  2026-11-5 【Pulse 快評｜ 中共真正懼怕的，是鏡子裡那個年輕的自己 （林兆彬）】 黃之鋒再被判囚十年，究竟中共在懼怕甚麼呢？答案是「學生運動」與「海外遊説」。這個恐懼是來自內在記憶，不少中共早期領導人都是學運出身，也長期「勾結」外國勢力蘇聯，在延安時期又遊說美國支持。中共清楚學生運動的力量，在今日學運領袖臉上，更看到自己年輕時的影子。革命成功之後，革命者最怕的，就是下一個革命者。 1919年五四運動，學生走到天安門，喊出「外爭國權，內除國賊」。那時候，張國燾是北京學聯領袖，周恩來在天津主編《學生聯合會報》、創立「覺悟社」。五四的核心其實是學生對權威的反抗，他們不相信政府，不相信條約，正是這種不信任，催生了後來的中共。 1935年的一二·九運動亦是如此，北平學生遊行反對華北自治。姚依林、黃華、蔣南翔學運領袖，後來都成了黨的高幹。姚依林做到政治局常委，副總理；黃華做到外交部長。甚至是江澤民，1940年代在南京中央大學、上海交大期間也積極參與學運，抗議國民黨政府各種政策。 中共害怕學運，因為它了解學運的核心是質疑體制。五四把矛頭指向北洋政府賣國，一二·九質疑國民黨的不抵抗，1989年批評中共腐敗。再者，學生一旦上街，未必會停在「反貪腐」的口號上。學生問更根本的問題：這個政權憑甚麼統治我們？ 學生有時間，有理想，有組織能力；最重要的是，他們還沒有被利益綁架，還相信「真理」，而中共也清楚「真理」是最危險的武器。 看看政府近年如何對待香港的大學。大約從2020年開始，它就不斷強化對大學的控制：校長言行越來越似黨委書記，學生會被消失。校園裡的言論被監控，社團被審查，連悼念宏福苑大火的活動都要經過批准。 那些在天安門廣場上絕食的學生和2019年參與社運的年輕人，與1919年火燒趙家樓的學生，其實很相似。他們都相信自己代表未來，都相信「國家興亡，匹夫有責」。中共知道這種信念一旦擴散，就會像野火一樣燒穿它辛苦建立的秩序。 ｜海外遊説觸動神經 為何中共對所謂「勾結外國勢力」如此敏感？因為他們深知，決定中國過去百年命運的關鍵正是外國勢力，親身體會過外國勢力怎樣改變中國的歷史進程，對於這種力量防範之嚴密，正是源於對自身崛起歷史的認知。 無論是國民黨還是共產黨，早期都深深烙印著「蘇聯基因」。孫中山向西方求援無果後，提出「聯俄容共」，引進蘇聯的資金、武器和列寧式的政黨組織模式，這才有了後來的黃埔軍校與北伐。而中共更是共產國際一手孵化的產物，是共產國際的中國支部，有些暴動會議都曾在蘇聯駐中國領事館內舉行，紅軍長征期間利用蘇聯科技破解國民黨的電報。 抗日戰爭結束後，美國的態度成為了決定中國命運的關鍵變數。當時的中共，為了打破國民黨的政治壟斷並爭取美國支援，在《新華日報》上發表了大量熱烈歌頌美國民主制度的文章。毛澤東在延安甚至向美國外交官明確表示，中國戰後的出路在於實行「美式民主」。 美國特使馬歇爾帶著政治幻想來到中國，試圖以西方的議會民主模式，強行將勢如水火的國共兩黨拉入「聯合政府」。1946年，國軍在東北戰場將林彪部隊打得節節敗退。馬歇爾為了迫蔣介石回到談判桌，以斷絕美援為威脅，強加「六月停戰令」。這給了中共軍隊寶貴的喘息與重組時機，徹底扭轉了東北戰局。 1948年美國總統大選，蔣介石政府因對民主黨時任總統杜魯門的對華武器禁運極度不滿，將籌碼全數押在共和黨候選人杜威身上。結果，杜魯門爆冷連任。不滿蔣介石政府貪污腐敗的杜魯門隨後發表《中美關係白皮書》，徹底中斷對蔣介石的實質援助。 美國當年在關鍵時刻的掣肘與最終的袖手旁觀，客觀上成為了壓垮國民黨政權的最後一根稻草。中國的命運，就這樣徹底滑向了另一個軌道。 中共怕學運，更怕遊説海外的學運，因為它清楚學運的可能性，它自己就是最好的例子。每當學生上街，中共就看到鏡子裡那個年輕的自己。那個自己已經死了，被權力埋葬了，但鏡子還在。

content: 来源：德正   Reuters, AFP, 法庭线等 黄之锋上月在狱中度过30岁生日。自2020年11月起，他已因不同案件在狱中还押超过2100天。 （德国之声中文网）香港民主运动代表人物、前香港众志秘书长黄之锋，週四（11月5日）被香港高等法院宣判，因违反香港《国家安全法》下的“串谋勾结外国势力”罪，判处10年监禁；目前因“47人案”正在服刑的黄之锋须服刑至2036年11月，出狱时或已40岁。 黄之锋上月在狱中度过30岁生日。自2020年11月起，他已因不同案件在狱中还押超过2100天。他去年6月被指控，与流亡海外的香港社运人士罗冠聪等人“串谋勾结外国势力危害国家安全”，在狱中被捕，并于今年9月承认该项控罪。但他表示，自己从未主张香港独立，也未曾寻求推翻中国政权。 “我也从未接受外国资金，或花钱聘请外国政治顾问。”黄之锋说。 港媒《法庭线》报道，黄之锋今日上午身穿蓝色深裇衫、咖啡色裤子、戴黑框眼镜，拿著书和一叠绿色簿子，走入法庭。该报记者表示，“法官宣判期间，黄之锋一度望向法庭的时钟，神情看似紧张，似是咬紧了牙。”《集志社》报道，黄之锋听闻判刑时表情平静，一直低头抄写。 主审法官谭耀豪指，被告黄之锋“罪行重大”。本案涉及的犯罪行为发生于2020年7月1日至11月23日之间，案发时香港正受社会动荡的严重影响，国家安全承受极高风险，被告与罗冠聪等人串谋，持续接触外国官员或机构，呼吁制裁中国及香港官员；在国安法实施后依然执行该计划，只是调整了两人的角色。法庭另外裁定，黄与罗为此案主谋。 港警国安处“欢迎重判” 人权组织吁“立即释放” 警方国安处总警司李桂华在宣判后向媒体表示，欢迎法庭重判，并指黄之锋从未成年时已开始参与社运，成年后“犯案累累”，不愿守法、不将法庭放在眼内。李桂华称，黄之锋案件有严重影响，尤其当时正值香港动荡时期，希望他“好好反省”。 人权组织“人权观察”发布声明，呼吁港府应立即无条件释放黄之锋、外国政府应谴责不当拘禁民运人士的判刑，并对负责官员实施制裁。 该组织亚洲部主任艾莲・皮尔逊（Elaine Pearson）表示：“以毫无根据的罪名对黄之锋判处如此严厉的刑罚，既残酷又不公正。” 今年2月，香港传媒大亨黎智英因勾结外国势力及煽动罪，被判处20年监禁。皮尔逊表示：“北京对香港日益加剧的打压，至今并未付出任何实质代价。” 台湾方面，陆委会声明批评中共及港府持续利用“港版国安法”等威权工具，对香港民主人士罗织罪名，进行无止尽的政治追诉。陆委会呼吁，即刻释放无辜遭拘押人士，保障港人应有的基本人权与言论自由。

title: Hong Kong lawmaker proposes digital ID checks for housing estate votes to combat bid-rigging
zh_title: 香港立法会议员提议对住宅区投票进行数字身份检查以打击串通投标
summary: 一名香港立法会议员建议在遗产会议上投票时使用政府管理的数字平台来验证业主的身份，这一措施旨在帮助防止未经授权的代理投票。宏福苑.照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。立法会议员方恭蕙周三在立法会会议上提出了打击串通投标的提案，串通投标是建筑维修行业的一种反竞争行为，在大埔公寓大楼发生致命火灾近一年后，香港领导人李家超已将其定为刑事犯罪。她的建议采取了这样的形式
content:
一名香港立法会议员建议在遗产会议上投票时使用政府管理的数字平台来验证业主的身份，这一措施旨在帮助防止未经授权的代理投票。宏福苑.照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。立法会议员方恭蕙周三在立法会会议上提出了打击串通投标的提案，串通投标是建筑维修行业的一种反竞争行为，在大埔公寓大楼发生致命火灾近一年后，香港领导人李家超已将其定为刑事犯罪。她的建议以议员议案的形式提出，该议案由议员提出，无意产生立法效力，但可能敦促政府采取具体措施。根据立法会文件，方建议研究利用政府的“iAM Smart”数字平台建立电子机制来核实和确认业主身份，“从而防止伪造、未经授权签署授权书以及滥用代理投票等问题。”未经授权的投票 2021 年 12 月的一次会议上进行的未经授权的代理投票帮助任命了宏福苑翻修工程的项目顾问，去年 11 月发生导致 168 人死亡、数千人流离失所的火灾时，该工程正在进行中。
项目顾问 Will Power Architects 此后被当局起诉，并与工程承包商 Prestige Construction & Engineering 一起被列为火灾背后的“罪魁祸首”之一。Christine Fong 于 2026 年 1 月 1 日宣誓就任香港立法会第八届任期。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。大约四分之一的代理选票是由时任区议员黄佩琪 (Peggy Wong) 收集的，她因在庄园中的角色受到指控以及缺席议会会议数月后于 9 月辞职。然而，根据调查的最终报告，向独立调查委员会提交的证据不足以证明她参与了大埔住宅区的串通投标。周三，曾任区议员的方议员在立法机关发表讲话时表示，她知道有人以当时身在海外的房主的名义在她所在地区的庄园进行投票，而他们并不知情。她在意见书中还敦促政府建立黑名单制度，禁止被判串标罪的当事人提交涉及公共资金和补贴的标书，以及须接受强制检查的建筑物项目。她还建议研究建立匿名电子招标系统，并利用人工智能和大数据建立招标“异常警报”系统。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong lawmaker has suggested using a government-managed digital platform to verify property owners’ identities when casting their ballots in estate meetings, a measure meant to help prevent unauthorised proxy voting. Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Lawmaker Christine Fong made the proposal at a Legislative Council (LegCo) meeting on Wednesday on combatting bid-rigging, an anti-competitive practice in the building maintenance industry that the city’s leader John Lee has moved to criminalise, almost a year after a deadly apartment complex fire in Tai Po. Her suggestion took the form of a member’s motion, a proposal introduced by a lawmaker that is not intended to have legislative effect but may urge the government to adopt specific measures. According to a LegCo document, Fong suggested looking into the use of the government’s “iAM Smart” digital platform to establish an electronic mechanism for verifying and confirming the identities of property owners, “thereby preventing issues such as forgery and unauthorized signing of powers of attorney and the abuse of proxy votes.” Unauthorised votes Unauthorised proxy votes cast at a December 2021 meeting helped appoint the project consultant for renovation works at Wang Fuk Court, which were ongoing at the time of the fire that killed 168 people and displaced thousands in November last year. Project consultant Will Power Architects has since been prosecuted by authorities and named as one of the “main culprits” behind the blaze, along with works contractor Prestige Construction & Engineering. Christine Fong is sworn in for the eighth term of Hong Kong’s Legislative Council on January 1, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. About a quarter of the proxy votes were collected by then-District Councillor Peggy Wong, who resigned from office in September amid allegations over her role at the estate and after months of absences from council meetings. However, evidence presented to an independent probe committee was insufficient to prove she was involved in bid-rigging at the Tai Po housing estate, according to the inquiry’s final report. Speaking at the legislature on Wednesday, lawmaker Fong, formerly a district councillor, said that she knew of votes being cast at estates in her district in the name of homeowners who were overseas at the time, without their knowledge. In her submission, she also urged the government to establish a blacklist system under which parties convicted of bid-rigging would be prohibited from submitting tenders involving public funds and subsidies, as well as projects for buildings subject to mandatory inspections. She also suggested looking into setting up an anonymised electronic tendering system and using artificial intelligence and big data to establish an “anomaly alert” system for tenders.

title: Australia scraps plan to sell Sydney military barracks after backlash
zh_title: 遭到强烈反对后，澳大利亚取消了出售悉尼军营的计划
summary: 遭到强烈反对后，澳大利亚放弃了出售悉尼军营的计划澳大利亚《海峡时报》在遭到强烈反对后取消了出售悉尼军营的计划立即注册：了解亚洲快速发展的发展 10 月 25 日，支持者和退伍军人参加反对联邦政府提议出售悉尼历史悠久的维多利亚军营的集会。发表于 2026 年 11 月 8 日上午 09:30 更新于 2026 年 11 月 8 日下午 03:07 澳大利亚将保留悉尼维多利亚军营和其他历史悠久的军营在出售 60 多处国防财产的计划遭到强烈反对后，军事基地落入公众手中。总理
content:
遭到强烈反对后，澳大利亚放弃了出售悉尼军营的计划海峡时报
遭到强烈反对后，澳大利亚取消了出售悉尼军营的计划
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
10 月 25 日，支持者和退伍军人在悉尼举行集会，反对联邦政府出售历史悠久的维多利亚军营的提议。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 8 日 09:30
更新于 2026 年 11 月 8 日 03:07 PM
在因出售 60 多处国防财产的计划遭到强烈反对后，澳大利亚将把悉尼维多利亚兵营和其他历史悠久的军事遗址保留在公众手中。
总理安东尼·阿尔巴内斯表示，军营“在我们国家的历史上占有特殊的地位”；国防部称其拥有“重要遗产”，其历史可以追溯到 1840 年。
随着澳大利亚对中国不断增强的军事实力做出反应，取消的销售预计将筹集 30 亿澳元，并帮助资助更强大的国防。
悉尼—在剥离未充分利用的国防财产的计划遭到强烈反对后，澳大利亚将保留包括悉尼军营在内的数个历史性军事遗址。
澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞 (Anthony Albanese) 11 月 8 日表示，政府出售全国 60 多个军事基地的提案将排除悉尼维多利亚军营等设施之一。
他说，该网站将保留在“公众手中”，并“供所有悉尼人使用”。
他说：“在对国防地产进行审查后确定的 67 个国防基地中，这是四个国防基地之一，这些国防基地将保留为公有制。”
阿尔巴尼斯说，其他禁止出售的地点包括墨尔本维多利亚兵营、维多利亚的昆斯克利夫堡和墨尔本边缘库克角的一处空军设施。
这一逆转是在寻求保护澳大利亚军事历史的团体对撤资努力提出批评之后发生的。
此次销售预计将产生 30 亿澳元（26.4 亿新元），这可能有助于为提高澳大利亚国防能力的计划提供资金，部分原因是为了应对中国不断增强的军事能力。
“我们面临着二战以来最复杂、在某些方面最具威胁的战略格局，因此我们的政府大幅增加了国防开支，”国防部长理查德·马勒斯在与阿尔巴内塞一起发言时说道。
Marles 表示，政府已将 67 个地点中的 11 个移交给财政部。

Australia will keep Victoria Barracks Sydney and other historic military sites in public hands after backlash over plans to sell more than 60 defence properties.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the barracks has “a special place in our nation’s history”; Defence says it has “significant heritage” and dates to 1840.
The scrapped sales were expected to raise A$3 billion and help fund stronger defence, as Australia responds to China’s rising military power.
SYDNEY – Australia will retain several historic military sites including barracks in Sydney, following a backlash over plans to divest underused defence properties.
Victoria Barracks Sydney is among a group of facilities that will be excluded from a government proposal to sell more than 60 military sites across the country, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Nov 8.
The site will remain in “public hands,” and be available “for all Sydneysiders to enjoy,” he said.
“This is one of four defence sites out of the 67 that were identified by the review into the defence estate that will be kept in public ownership,” he said.
Other sites to be shielded from sale include Victoria Barracks Melbourne, Fort Queenscliff in Victoria and an air force facility in Point Cook on Melbourne’s fringe, Albanese said.
The reversal follows criticism of the divestment efforts from groups seeking to preserve Australia’s military history.
The sales will generate an estimated A$3 billion (S$2.64 billion), which could help fund plans to increase Australia’s defence capacity, partly in response to China’s rising military capabilities.
“We face the most complex, in some ways the most threatening strategic landscape that we have faced since the Second World War and as a result of that our government has significantly increased defence expenditure,” said Minister for Defence Richard Marles, speaking alongside Albanese.
The government has transferred 11 of the 67 sites to the Department of Finance, Marles said.
The Sydney barracks was established in 1840 and initially housed the British Army, according to Australia’s Defence department, which attributes “significant heritage” to the site. BLOOMBERG

当骑车人在夜间刹车时，背心还会闪烁红光。
另一枚金牌则颁给了台东东海国中的一名学生，他们的产品是一款配备放大镜和智能分析功能的多功能指甲修剪盒。
该设备分析用户的指甲和指甲剪，以提供个性化的健康建议。

台湾护理品牌O'right Inc.开发的一款基于咖啡因和黑色素的头皮活化洗发水也获得了金奖。
该产品旨在护理白发，不使用 TIA 所说的传统染发剂中常见的五种主要潜在有害成分。

Taiwanese inventors wins at the 2026 iENA International Trade Fair-Ideas-Inventions-New Products in Nuremberg, Germany. Photo courtesy of the Taiwan Invention Association
Berlin, Nov. 7 (CNA) Taiwanese inventors won 12 gold medals, 15 silver medals and 23 bronze medals at the 2026 iENA International Trade Fair-Ideas-Inventions-New Products in Nuremberg, Germany, the Taiwan Invention Association (TIA) said.
The TIA led a delegation of 78 inventors at the event.
Among the gold medal winners were students from Feng-tian Junior High School in Taitung County, who received the award for a smart safety vest for cyclists that is equipped with lights that signal a cyclist's intended direction of travel.
The signals can be activated manually using a wireless button mounted on the bicycle's handlebar or automatically through integration with Google Maps, which activates the appropriate signal before a turn, according to the TIA.
The vest also flashes a red light when the cyclist brakes at night.
Another gold medal went to a student from Tung Hai Junior High School, also in Taitung, for a multifunctional nail-trimming box equipped with a magnifying glass and smart analysis features.
The device analyzes users' nails and nail clippings to provide personalized health suggestions.
Students from St. Joseph Technical Senior High School in Taitung won a gold medal for a height-adjustable urinal.
Students from St. Joseph Technical Senior High School in Taitung display their gold-medal-winning height-adjustable urinal at the 2026 iENA International Trade Fair, Ideas-Inventions-New Products, in Nuremberg, Germany. Photo courtesy of the Taiwan Invention Association
The urinal uses infrared sensors to detect users' height and adjust accordingly. Its retractable drainage pipe and safety features are designed to reduce urine splashing and improve hygiene in public restrooms.
A caffeine- and melanin-based scalp-revitalizing shampoo developed by Taiwanese care brand O'right Inc. also won a gold medal.
The product is designed to care for graying hair without using what the TIA described as five major potentially harmful ingredients commonly found in traditional hair dyes.
Speaking of the competition, TIA Chairwoman Chang Chia-chu (張家菊) said education should focus not only on imparting knowledge but also on cultivating independent thinking, innovation and practical problem-solving skills.
The 2026 iENA fair was held in Nuremberg from Oct. 31 to Nov. 2, featuring 580 inventions presented by 340 exhibitors from 21 countries and regions, according to the event's official website.

title: AI热潮带动资料中心扩建　印尼巴淡岛缺水惹民怨

content:
（法新社印尼巴淡岛8日电） 在印尼巴淡岛，随着一座座资料中心拔地而起，为全球人工智慧（AI）热潮提供支援，当地自来水却面临枯竭，连做饭与洗澡都变得十分困难，引发当地居民发起抗议。

发表时间： 08/11/2026 - 08:32

6 分钟 浏览时间

当地自来水营运商告诉法新社，这个地区因降雨量偏低，长期饱受干旱之苦，强烈的圣婴现象更使干燥情况加剧。

不过，与其他国家情况相同，资料中心也引发民众不满。这类设施外观类似仓库，负责维持各种应用程式及AI工具运作，且往往需要大量用水来冷却运转中的伺服器。 印尼和马来西亚民众的不满情绪日益升高，尤其是在与新加坡接壤、被视为兴建新科技设施的优先地点。

54岁的技工朱尼亚迪（Juniardi Adinda Sembiring Gurukinayan）告诉法新社，起初当地民众的主要反应是「感谢上天，巴淡岛终于有产业进驻了。」

但近期巴淡岛部分社区的自来水服务频繁严重中断，导致他「有时甚至只好不洗澡」。

他说：「没有水，我们就无法煮饭，也不能煮蔬菜。」

在情况最严重的时候，数十名愤怒居民自发前往农沙数位园区（Nongsa Digital Park）外抗议。这座由资料中心及其他设施组成的新兴聚落，已被划定为经济特区。

朱尼亚迪指出，当地居民认为，「缺水问题…与资料中心的兴建有关」。 自来水公司巴Air Batam Hilir发言人金达（Ginda Alamsyah）表示，干旱导致附近的农沙水库（Nongsa Reservoir）水位大幅下降，供水系统又因电力故障进一步受到影响。

根据KPMG安侯建业一份报告，受AI使用量暴增10倍带动，东南亚资料中心的容量预计到2030年将达到2025年的3倍。

这可能对供水造成压力，也让仍严重依赖暖化地球之化石燃料的电网面临严峻考验。

印尼和马来西亚的资料中心兴建热潮，始于高度联网的新加坡受资源限制影响，于2019年至2022年间暂停核准新的资料中心开发案。

此后，两国资料中心建设加速，政府与科技巨头投入数千亿美元，用于训练及运行AI，带动两国经济成长。

金达表示，Air Batam Hilir支持鼓励在巴淡岛投资与发展的政策。巴淡岛位于新加坡南方、并透过海底电缆与新加坡相连。

但他也指出，必须妥善管理用水需求。他补充说，Air Batam Hilir正透过疏浚作业，提高巴淡岛6座水库的蓄水能力，干旱期间也可考虑采取人工造雨的措施。

title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang officially called to Congress due to reports of a Chinese spy plot
zh_title: 英伟达的黄仁勋因有关中国间谍阴谋的报道而正式向国会发出呼吁
summary: Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 是一个经常参加大量会议的人，今天他繁忙的日程中又增加了一次会议。美国国会希望就国家安全日益加剧的担忧与黄进行闭门会谈。争取他的时间的国会议员表示，上周的报告促使他可能成为据报道的中国资产间谍活动的目标：Megaspeed 执行官 Alice Huang（与家人无关）。深入了解 TH Premium：人工智能和数据中心（图片来源：微软） 数据中心冷却现状 定制 AI ASIC 现状 美国的人工智能芯片规则保持着领先地位
content:
Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 是一个经常参加大量会议的人，今天他繁忙的日程中又增加了一次会议。美国国会希望就国家安全日益加剧的担忧与黄进行闭门会谈。争取他的时间的国会议员表示，上周的报告促使他可能成为据报道的中国资产间谍活动的目标：Megaspeed 执行官 Alice Huang（与家人无关）。深入了解 TH Premium：AI 和数据中心（图片来源：Microsoft） 数据中心冷却现状 定制 AI ASIC 现状 美国的 AI 芯片规则不断变化 - 世界其他地区正在付出代价 GTC 2026：Ian Buck 新闻问答记录 - 超大规模和 HPC 副总裁就今年搁置 CPX 和运输 LPU 解码发表讲话 对数据中心 CPU 的需求激增，AI 代理负责 该会议由共和党众议院代表 John 组织穆勒纳尔、布莱恩·马斯特和里克·克劳福德分别担任众议院中国委员会、外交事务委员会和情报委员会主席。在众议院关于此事的信函中，议员们表示，上述报道“引发了对中国获取美国技术和信息的重大国家安全担忧”。此前报道的说法是，Alice Huang 是新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的中国工厂，正在向北京窃取信息。
《华尔街日报》进一步声称，她因与黄仁勋的现有关系而被中国当局招募。 据《纽约时报》报道，Megaspeed 购买并继续购买价值数十亿美元的 Nvidia 芯片，并自 2024 年以来被美国商务部指控向中国走私价值 20 亿美元的先进芯片。这种情况的背景是，美国长期以来实行出口管制，阻止英伟达和AMD最先进的人工智能加速器芯片进入中国和其他一些国家。这些指控上周首次在《纽约时报》上发表，据报道来自未透露姓名的美国情报官员。众议院表示，与黄仁勋举行简报的目的是讨论“英伟达针对外国对手间谍活动的安全协议以及[他]与[...]爱丽丝·黄的互动。”据《纽约时报》报道，首席执行官从未收到过“防御简报”，本质上是对外国间谍活动的潜在目标的警告，让他们熟悉此类活动的迹象。该出版物指出，情报官员常常不愿告知潜在的间谍目标，因为这样做可能会让间谍意识到他们正在接受调查。 《纽约时报》补充说，特朗普总统一年前曾获悉有关 Megaspeed 和 Alice Huang 的情况，但选择不采取行动。
据《华尔街日报》报道，新加坡当局对 Megaspeed 展开了自己的调查，甚至据报道直接询问了 Alice Huang。不过，该国的官方回应告诉《华尔街日报》，新加坡“不执行外国司法管辖区实施的单方面出口管制”，并补充说，在调查 Megaspeed 时，并不是针对 Alice Huang 本人，也不是检查她声称与黄仁勋或中国的关系。 《新加坡人》确实指出，该国对商业欺诈采取“零容忍立场”，并指出该国已因此类不当行为对四家公司和四名个人提出指控，他们可能面临最高 20 年的监禁。与此同时，台湾似乎也在密切关注A

【原文 English Original】
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is a man who likely attends numerous meetings, and today one more was added to his busy schedule. The U.S. Congress wants to have a closed-door chat with Huang over mounting concerns about national security. The congressmen bidding for his time say last week's report spurred the move that he may be the target of espionage by a reported Chinese asset: Megaspeed exec Alice Huang (family unrelated). Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft) The data center cooling state of play The custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the price GTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this year Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible The meeting was set up by Republican House representatives John Moolenaar, Brian Mast, and Rick Crawford, respective Chairs of the House committees on China, Foreign Affairs, and Intelligence. In the House's letter on the matter, the lawmakers say the aforementioned reports "raise significant national security concerns" about China gaining access to U.S. technology and information. The previously reported claim is that Alice Huang is a Chinese plant in Singaporean data center outfit Megaspeed, siphoning information to Beijing. The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) further claims that she was recruited by Chinese authorities due to her existing relationship with Jensen Huang. Megaspeed reportedly bought and continues to buy billions' worth of Nvidia's chips, according to The New York Times (NYT), and stands accused by the Department of Commerce since 2024 of smuggling $2 billion worth of advanced silicon to China. The backdrop for the situation is that the U.S. has long-standing export controls blocking Nvidia and AMD's most advanced AI accelerator chips from reaching China, among a number of other nations. The allegations were first published last week in the NYT, and are reportedly sourced from unnamed U.S. intelligence officials. The House says the purpose of the briefing with Jensen Huang is to discuss "Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and [his] interactions with [...] Alice Huang." According to the NYT, the CEO never got a "defensive briefing," essentially a warning for potential targets of foreign espionage, to acquaint them with signs of such activities. The publication notes that intelligence officials often hesitate to inform potential targets of espionage, as doing so may make the spy aware they're being investigated. The NYT adds that President Trump was briefed on the situation surrounding Megaspeed and Alice Huang a year ago, but chose not to act on it. According to the WSJ, Singaporean authorities opened their own probe into Megaspeed, and even reportedly questioned Alice Huang directly. However, an official response from the country told the WSJ that it "does not implement unilateral export controls imposed by foreign jurisdictions," adding that while it's investigating Megaspeed, it's not targeting Alice Huang herself or inspecting her claimed ties with Jensen Huang or China. The Singaporean does note that the country has "a zero-tolerance stance" on commercial fraud, pointing out that it's charged four companies and four individuals over such wrongdoings, and that they may face up to 20 years in prison. Meanwhile, Taiwan is also seemingly keeping a close eye on Alice Huang, by inspecting her visits to the nation. The WSJ says that the country's authorities are probing her involvement with China and have her under physical surveillance. As for Nvidia, the company seemingly reposted today the same comments it offered us last week, stating that "meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year." The firm adds that "[its] regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security."

Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo
A memo circulated earlier this year claimed that technology executive Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports.
The New York Times, which had previously said Nvidia’s chief executive had been the target of Chinese intelligence, was the first to report on the memo, which was reportedly based on U.S. intelligence. The Financial Times subsequently reported that the memo also claimed Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed.
An Nvidia spokesperson told the NYT that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with its customers.
A separate NYT report examined New Matrix, a Chinese company authorized by the U.S. Commerce Department to buy advanced Nvidia chips. But at the office address listed by New Matrix, reporters only found “a hollow gray shell,” raising concerns that it could be a front for a blacklisted private equity firm.
The Nvidia spokesperson said the company sells “the first, best and most of our technology in America.”
